info.title: OpenAsy Automation API
info.summary: Playbooks that act through the products when one of them sees something, with approvals before risky steps.
info.description:
Every screen of automation uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Events start playbooks at `/hooks/<playbook>`, with the playbook's own token. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.summary: Send an event to a playbook
post.description:
Starts a playbook whose trigger is a webhook, when its conditions hold on the event. The body is the event, any JSON object up to 256 KiB.

```bash
curl -sf -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"signal":{"rule":"impossible-travel","person":"p_ada"}}' https://automation.example.com/hooks/pb_…
```

200.description: The conditions do not hold: no run.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when automation runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the automation origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_automation_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when automation is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

webhookToken.description: A playbook's own token (`oah_…`), shown when its webhook trigger is made. It starts that playbook and nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

product.description: For an OpenAsy connection, the product's id, such as incidents.

address.description: A product's address; of Slack, Teams and webhooks only the host, as the rest of the URL is a key.

playbooks.description: Playbooks with a step that uses it.

product.description: For openasy: the product's id. Built-in steps need incidents or vpn; http steps take any.

url.description: A product's address, or the webhook URL Slack, Teams or a tool gave. https, except on this machine.

token.description: For openasy: an API token of that product, with the role the steps need. Kept sealed, never shown again.

field.description: A path in the event, such as signal.severity.

Step.description: One step. Text fields are templates: {{event.…}}, {{steps.<id>.…}} for the answer of an earlier step, {{run.id}}, {{playbook.name}}. incident.open needs title (severity, summary); incident.note incident and text; vpn.suspend person; vpn.disconnect server and device; vpn.revoke-device device; message text; http method, path and an optional JSON body; approval text.

connection.description: A connection's id; approval takes none.

path.description: After the connection's address; it can never leave it.

conditions.description: All must hold on the event; none means every event.

webhookToken.description: Shown once, when a webhook trigger gets a token.

event.description: The event to run on, as a trigger would send it.

dry.description: Send nothing; show what would be sent.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as cursor for the next page.

request.description: What was sent, without the token; for an approval, the question.

response.description: The status and the answer, at most 16,000 characters.

definition.description: The steps as they were when the run started.

last30Days.description: Runs of the last 30 days, dry runs left out.
